messages:
Maya: FYI perf alert this morning after the continuous-batching tweak - p95 on gpt-mids went up ~120ms and cache hit-rate dropped from 78% -> 61% :eyes:
Sam: ugh, saw the same on the dashboard. timeline aligns with the deploy at 03:10 UTC. link: https://console.redwood/perf/dashboards/prefix-cache?range=6h
Alex: Quick summary from local profiling: when batch-mixer switched to slice-first packing the per-request kernel selection jumped to the slower ATTN path for ~30% of requests, which increases token-time and prevents timely KV warmups. paste of profiler snippet:
```
kernel_choice_hist: {fast_attn: 68, dense_attn: 32}
kv_warmup_latency_ms: median=6.1 p95=42.3
cache_lookup_miss_rate: 0.39
average_batch_size: 7.2 -> 9.8 (post-deploy)
```
Sam: that miss_rate (0.39) matches the hit-rate drop Maya saw. My hypothesis: bigger mixed batches increase interleaving of distinct prefixes so prefix-cache keys aren't seeing enough contiguous warmup to be useful.
Jia: Also noticed queueing jitter increased. The continuous batching window had its max_delay bumped from 8ms -> 15ms in the rollout PR. That gives more time to coalesce but also makes cohort boundaries blur.
Otto: Related note: when batch size rises we sometimes switch kernel config to the throughput-optimized schedule which disables inline KV prefetch in the runtime path — that would explain both miss and kernel shift.
Maya: can someone point to the exact commit? I want to triage the rollout flags.
deploy-bot: Deployed by @sam at 2024-11-12T03:10:21Z — PR #4829 — continuous-batch: increase max_delay to 15ms; enable slice-first packing on mixed workloads.
Sam: PR #4829 is it. Reverting max_delay to 8ms brought hit-rate back to ~75% in a canary earlier today. I ran a short ab to confirm (see results below).
```
canary results (10m):
- baseline deploy: p50=14ms p95=42ms cache_hit=0.78
- pr4829: p50=18ms p95=62ms cache_hit=0.61
- pr4829 + revert max_delay: p50=15ms p95=45ms cache_hit=0.74
```
Alex: Nice. So it's not only packing policy but the increased queuing time allowing heterogeneous requests to merge. Two knobs: max_delay and the batching affinity key.
Jia: affinity key = prefix-hash now. If we change to prefix-hash+route or reduce prefix-hash entropy (cohort rounding) we can increase contiguous hits. Example config suggestion:
```
batching:
  max_delay_ms: 8
  affinity_key: "prefix_cohort_v2"  # round hash to 64 buckets
  slice_packing: false
```
Otto: We should also consider warming policy: when a request sees a cache miss, the runtime could spawn a high-priority warmup task to populate adjacent KV slots for the same cohort. That trades CPU but should reduce miss storms.
Maya: Good idea. Any quick telemetry to estimate cost of eager warmups?
Alex: From last year we have a warming job estimate: warmup CPU per 1k warmups = ~0.12 vCPU-min. If we reduce miss-rate by 10% it pays off for high-throughput models.
Sam: Action items I propose:
1) revert max_delay to 8ms in prod (done in canary earlier, schedule full revert) - owner: Sam
2) roll a small experiment with affinity_key = prefix_cohort_v2 (64 buckets) in staging - owner: Jia
3) prototype eager-warmup (priority task) behind a feature flag and run burst tests - owner: Otto
4) add a perf regression alert that correlates kernel_choice_hist + cache_miss_rate so we get earlier signals - owner: Alex
Maya: I'll create the incident ticket and coordinate rollback if any canary shows regression.
Sam: I'll open the revert PR and link to these notes.
Jia: I'll add the affinity experiment to the staging config and schedule a 2-hour run tomorrow morning.
Otto: I'll stub the warmup flag and add simple telemetry counters so we can evaluate cost.
Alex: I'll wire the dashboard alert and a quick Jenkins job to capture kernel_choice_hist every 5s for 30m after deploys.
Maya: Thanks team. Short-term rollback looks safe; long-term we want smarter packing that respects prefix locality. Will follow up in eng-runtime async thread with a design doc. :thumbsup:
Sam: ping me if anyone needs the canary logs or the exact profiler trace, I saved them under /mnt/profiler/2024-11-12/pr4829.trace
Maya: closing the loop — created ticket INF-8793 and linked PRs. We'll reconvene after the staging run.
